title: Gouache for Beginners: The Series!
description:
this is a three part gouache painting series ideal for absolute beginners and curious creatives hosted on Tuesdays, June 16, 23, and 30 from 7 pm - 9 pm.

we will explore how gouache behaves and learn that there is no “right” way to paint, that we can create beautiful, personal, and expressive pieces with this unique medium.

June 16: Basic Techniques - experiment with layering, consistency, and color blending to complete a small painting with a simple subject (think a piece of fruit or a flower)

June 23: Building Depth -  learn how to build up layers of light and shadow to create contrast and depth with a simple still life with a few objects (think a bowl of fruit or flowers in a vase)

June 30: Composition - paint the same subject from different perspectives and interpretations to create unique, expressive pieces 

All materials and supplies are provided and all levels are welcome - no prior painting experience required.

Facilitated by recess grove co-creator jessie spellman

title: Beginner Woodshop
description: An approachable, hands-on intro to hand tool woodworking at recess grove. Learn how to use a hand saw, chisel, block plane, and other carving tools, along with the core measuring and marking tools. Get a taste for the foundational skills as you as you cut and carve wood on our classic workbenches. Begin your woodworking journey through a focus on tools, methods, and mindset.

title: Mending Skillz: Darning!
description:
got a hole in your sock? looking to add mending techniques to your repertoire of fiber skills?

come to this quick fiber clinic to learn a basic mending skill – darning!

darning is mending technique that uses a needle and thread to repair holes and worn areas in soft garments that results in a woven pattern. darning can be used to repair socks, sweaters, and even larger damage in woven or knitted fabrics.

*bring any garment with a hole you're trying to mend - scraps for practice will be provided*

hosted by local artist, andrea herrada during our free soft craft circle.

feel free to stick around after and mingle with other crafters while working on these newfound skills!

title: Your Year of Creativity: Building a Creative Practice
description:
we are in a creative renaissance: there are classes and events to learn a new skill, find a hobby, reconnect with our inner child, take ourselves on something called an ‘artist date’ — but where do you even begin?! 

join us for cozy hangs all year long to inspire your creative flow and build your own creative practice

we'll guide you through prompts and intention setting while you play with paint, pencil, and polymer clay

if you're not sure how to begin creating but you're ready to explore your creativity, this is a great place to start in a low-pressure and encouraging environment

hosted the third Thursday of each month by recess grove co-creators jessie spellman, Corey Belaief, and Justin Wheeler

title: Garden: Flower Pounding
description:
pick your own flora from the garden using the principles of honorable harvest 

transfer the vibrant colors and patterns onto cloth or paper with the magic of flower pounding

watch the pigments burst with each tap of your hammer, revealing designs unique as each flower

all flower pounding supplies included, including unlimited watercolor paper 

if you bring your own cotton fabric, we recommend you pre treat it first by soaking the fabric in a solution with a 1:16 ratio of alum to water for at least 2 and up to 24 hours. once the fabric has soaked, wash it on a rinse only cycle in the washing machine (or rinse in a bathtub or sink with clean water) and let it air dry

title: Cyanotype: sun printing
description:
discover the magic of cyanotype and create stunning prints using the sun! In this beginner-friendly workshop, students will learn how to coat cyanotype paper and make prints using the power of the sun as a source of exposure.

the cyanotype process uses a chemical mixture that creates characteristically blue-and-white images when exposed to UV light and washed in water. perfect for anyone looking for a new creative outlet, this class offers a unique way to experiment with art, science, and nature.

all materials will be provided, but participants are welcome to bring any textured objects they wish to experiment with printing. (e.g. lace, textured glass, leaves, flowers, film negatives)

hosted by local artist  Delaney Accomando

title: How to Talk Politics Well, Effectively, and Pro-Socially
Dreams and the Emotional Subconscious: A Creative Writing Seminar
description:
What lives in your subconscious has always wanted to become a story.

In this four-week short story seminar hosted by native New York artist, writer, and director Alix Marello we draw on Jungian theory and magical realist writers to explore the landscapes of dream, symbol, emotion, and the subconscious. Over the course, you'll write, workshop, and refine one complete short story.

Each student will receive a notebook. We write by hand here — no laptops, please. Come ready to put pen to paper.

All levels of experience are welcome.

* These classes will take place from 6:30 pm - 9:00 pm over 4 consecutive Tuesday evenings in July *

Week 1: July 7 - Introductions, Dream Sharing and Interpretations

Week 2: July 14 - Dream Journals, Reverse Dreaming

Week 3: July 21 - Feedback and Editing

Week 4: July 28 -  Reflections and Discussion

* artist bio *
Alix holds an MFA in Screenwriting from the University of Southern California and a BA in English from Skidmore College. A recent Millay Arts Fellow, she used the residency to complete a short story collection, and she currently serves as the founder of the visual and literary arts magazine Etchings Press. During her time at USC, she received an academic mentorship with Celine Song, writer and director of the Oscar-nominated filmPast Lives.

Her screenwriting work has earned notable recognition: her feature-length screenplay was selected for the Austin Film Festival in fall 2024, and her short film reached the semi-finals of ScreenCraft's 2025 competition. On the theatrical side, she was commissioned to write two plays for Saratoga Performing Arts Center and served as a staff writer for an Amazon Prime television series.

Alix is also the recipient of David Letterman's playwriting residency, through which her work was exhibited at the Metropolitan Museum of Art and performed off-Broadway. Her writing has been recognized with several national honors and she was selected as a storyteller for NPR'sThe Moth.

title: Songs You Can Touch: Live Music and Visual Art Making
description:
Celebrate Cancer szn with an interactive concert at recess grove led by singer-songwriters, facilitators and July birthday babes Ben Freeman and Emma Jayne!

You'll hear songs from each artist (expect us to go big on the Cancer feels) and be invited to draw, collage, and paint what you hear. We'll make up new songs together and find improvised ways to put our music and visual art making into conversation. We'll also pause between sets to get to know each other through creative prompts and whimsical participatory art. Leave more in touch with your feelings, a shifted perspective on your own making, and some new friends to boot.

Songs You Can Touch is a That's Interesting! experience.
All art supplies included!

--

About the artists:

Ben Freeman (he/him) is an interactive artist, performer, and experience designer. As a musician, he sings with the New York Vocal Collective, has released two EPs and a full-length album, and is working toward releasing his second full-length album, starting with the single "Henrietta's Treasures." As a facilitator and experience designer, he is the founder and lead facilitator of That's Interesting! — a studio for the playful practice of attention. That's Interesting! hosts art parties, interactive performances, workshops, and ensemble experiences at the intersection of play as a spiritual practice and as a form of attention activism. @bshatteredbfree @thatsintersting.studio

Emma Jayne (they/she) is an Emmy-nominated composer, singer-songwriter, and comedian based in Brooklyn, NY. With 3M+ streams across 15 releases, Emma's music has garnered placements on Spotify editorial playlists like Fresh Finds Pop. Notable achievements include composing for Hallmark and Coca-Cola, and winning Jimmy Fallon's 'Battle of the Instant Songwriters' on The Tonight Show.  Emma has collaborated with and opened for bands like Lawrence, Leah Marlene, Couch, Erez Zobary, and Sense.

For lovers of Carole King, Sara Bareilles, and laughing until you cry, Emma’s music has an Adult Contemporary sensibility with Pop-Soul listenability. Their artistry is about connection, possibility, and authenticity. Emma is dedicated to modeling honest, committed, and unapologetically queer songwriting for the next generation. 
In addition to music, Emma empowers LGBTQIA+ youth as the co-founder of Future Perfect Records, a residency for queer youth musicians through the non-profit The Future Perfect Project. Currently, Emma is working on her second album, fueled in part by the Music Forward Foundation's LGBTQ+ Emerging Artist Award
